sections.html:
Greer straddles the Greenville and Spartanburg county line, about 12 miles northeast of Greenville and 17 miles west of Spartanburg. A 2023 estimate puts about 25,587 residents in Greenville County and 9,721 in Spartanburg County. The 2025 estimate for the whole city is 50,007, up from 35,308 in the 2020 census.

Sellers underestimate that boundary. Whichever county holds your parcel supplies the assessor, the treasurer and the Register of Deeds. Schools follow the same split: Greenville County residents are served by the Greenville County School District, and some Spartanburg County addresses fall in Spartanburg School District 5. Check your tax notice before you start. Spartanburg County addresses go through that county's offices, and Greenville County addresses go through Greenville's, so calling the wrong office wastes a day.

Most Greer homes are lived in by their owners, and the city keeps growing. Here are area medians covering 2020 to 2024.

Housing measureGreer
Owner-occupied housing rate72.7%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$288,700
Median gross rent$1,198

An average tells you nothing about your own house. If yours needs a roof and a new kitchen, it will not fetch the median price, because a cash buyer counts the cost of the work.

A railroad stop started Greer, and textile mills built it up. The result is a mix of mill-era blocks around the old center and subdivisions farther out. Owners of the older houses often face postponed repairs, which is one reason they turn to as-is sales.

Jobs also drive moves. Manufacturing and logistics carry the local economy along I-85, including a large BMW plant and Inland Port Greer, a 91 acre container hub at 100 International Commerce Blvd. People move here for those jobs and leave for others, and a job transfer with a short deadline is a common reason to want a fast closing instead of a months-long listing.

sections.h2: Weather wear on an older house
sections.html:
Hot, humid summers and short, mild winters define the year. July highs average 90.3 degrees, and the area gets about 49.67 inches of precipitation a year plus 3.9 inches of snow. That is enough rain to find every weak flashing, clogged gutter and low grade near a foundation, and enough heat to shorten an old HVAC system's life. Look over these before listing or accepting an offer:

  • Roof age and missing or lifted shingles
  • Stains from water in attics, crawl spaces or beneath windows
  • HVAC units near the end of their service life
  • Drainage around houses close to the lakes or the South Tyger River

Apalache Lake, Lake Robinson and Lake Cunningham lie inside or beside the city. If your house backs up to water, mention it early, and ask the county floodplain office for the mapped zone before you set a price.

Which county holds the house decides the bill, and a sale can move the assessed value. Under Section 12-43-220, a legal residence (the owner's home plus up to five acres) is assessed at 4%, and all other real estate at 6%. An owner later found ineligible falls back to 6% and can face a penalty of 100% of the tax paid plus 0.5% interest per month.

In Greenville County, a qualifying sale is an assessable transfer of interest. The home is reassessed at market value as of December 31 of the sale year, and the 15% cap on increases no longer applies. Whoever buys must file a fresh application for the 4% rate by January 15 after the ownership change.

Bills can be paid from September 30 through January 15. Under Section 12-45-180, late bills pick up 3% after January 15, 7% more after February 1 and 5% more after March 16. In Greenville County, January 15 also closes the appeal window for the previous year's values, and bills typically mail toward the end of October.

For a Greenville County parcel, the Register of Deeds records the deed from Suite S-2100 at Greenville County Square, 301 University Ridge. Doors are open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and those recording in person are asked to come before 4:30 p.m.

Section 12-24-90 sets the state fee at $1.85 per $500 of value or fraction, of which $1.30 is the state's share and $0.55 the county's. Exemptions include a deed to a mortgagee in lieu of foreclosure and deeds that merely confirm title already held, with no payment. The county schedule covers any other office fees.

After scanning, the office hands the originals back. Clerks do not offer legal advice, and they recommend consulting a legal professional before you draft a deed on your own.

Every rental inside the city has to be registered and hold a city rental license for its classification. Selling a rental? Make sure the license is current and the tenant situation is settled before an inspection.

The Community Standards Division, listed as Community Compliance, handles code enforcement. The city office is at 301 E. Poinsett Street, phone (864) 848-2150. Ask about open violations on your address, since an unresolved complaint can slow a conventional sale when lenders and buyers want a clean record.

Some chores shorten a Greer sale. Photograph repairs you have already made. Dig out permit records, because lenders and buyers prefer a tidy paper trail. If a tenant lives there, schedule showings with notice and ask whether they plan to stay.

Think about whether the nearby lake or river helps your sale. A water view draws some buyers, while others fret about drainage and insurance. Share the flood zone early and an inspection is less likely to produce a surprise.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like
sections.html:
Selling for cash in Greer removes the mortgage approval that so often delays a closing. Ask for an offer, the buyer looks at the house as it is, and you set a closing date that suits you.

  • No need to clean, stage or fix the roof, HVAC or flooring first
  • Inherited, tenant-occupied, mill-era and vacant houses are all fair game
  • A deed, a title company and the county recording steps above still apply
  • You can decline the offer and owe nothing

To get a firm offer sooner, hand the buyer your tax bill, mortgage payoff figure, any lease and the names on the deed. The attorney can begin title work as soon as those arrive.

faqs.q: How big is Greer, SC, and what counties is it in?
faqs.a: Greer covers 25.56 square miles and sits in both Greenville and Spartanburg counties. About 12 miles separate it from Greenville and about 17 miles from Spartanburg.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with if I sell a house in Greer?
faqs.a: The one that holds your parcel, since Greer straddles two counties. That county handles the assessment, tax bill and deed recording, so check your tax notice first.

faqs.q: When are South Carolina property taxes due on a Greer home?
faqs.a: State law makes them due between September 30 and January 15. Penalties start the day after January 15 at 3%, then another 7% after February 1 and 5% after March 16.

faqs.q: Does selling my Greer house raise the property tax?
faqs.a: It can for the buyer. Greenville County treats a qualifying sale as an assessable transfer that reassesses the home at current market value and ends the 15% cap, and the new owner must apply for the 4% rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Greer house with code violations or tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a house with open issues or tenants in place, though clearing or disclosing violations and confirming the city rental license makes the closing smoother.
